paper_b.title: Improved Approximation Algorithms for Maximum Cut and Satisfiability Problems Using Semidefinite Programming

metadata.description: The pair was curated as 'Goemans vs Feige-Goemans' (SDP rounding) but paper A is in fact Hastad's 'Some Optimal Inapproximability Results' (PCP-based NP-hardness of approximation) while paper B is Goemans-Williamson's 0.878 SDP approximation for MAX CUT (and related MAX 2SAT, MAX DICUT). The two papers attack the SAME problems (MAX CUT, MAX 2SAT, MAX DICUT, MAX SAT) from opposite, complementary angles: Hastad establishes NP-hardness lower bounds (17/16 for MAX CUT, 22/21 for MAX-E2-SAT, 13/12 for MAX DICUT, 7/8 for MAX-3-SAT, 2 for MAX-E3-LIN-2) while Goemans-Williamson establishes matching algorithmic upper bounds (alpha~0.87856 for MAX CUT, alpha for MAX 2SAT, beta>0.79607 for MAX DICUT). The conceptual machinery is wholly different (Long-code PCP / Fourier analysis vs SDP relaxation / random hyperplane rounding), so the relationship is best classified as CF (competing frameworks, complementary results on the same problems). Both papers are PDF-fallback extractions; trust names/types over LaTeX statements.

matches.explanation: Both papers define the standard MAX CUT problem (find a vertex partition maximizing the weight/number of crossing edges). Paper A frames it as a definition ('Max-Cut'), paper B as a problem ('MAX CUT problem') with weighted edges; the underlying object is identical.

Both define the directed-cut variant (MAX DICUT / Max-di-Cut): partition the vertices of a directed graph and count/weight arcs whose tail lies in V_1 and head in V_2. Same problem up to weighted vs unweighted formulation.

Paper A's Max-Ek-Sat (E_k-CNF satisfaction maximization) and paper B's MAX SAT problem are essentially the same problem, with paper A specializing to clauses of length exactly k and paper B treating arbitrary-length weighted clauses. Tagged 'analogous' because of the Ek vs general-length distinction; both paper-origin problem statements about maximizing satisfied clauses.

Paper B's MAX 2SAT problem (length-<=2 clauses, weighted) is the object whose hardness Hastad addresses in TP365.17 (Max-E2-Sat inapproximability within 22/21). The match aligns paper B's problem definition with paper A's hardness theorem on it, which is the natural cross-paper correspondence.

Complementary MAX CUT bounds. Hastad's TP365.26 proves it is NP-hard to approximate Max-Cut within 17/16 - epsilon (i.e., any factor smaller than 16/17 ~ 0.941). Goemans-Williamson's AP366.1 / TP366.3.3 / CP366.5.1 give a polynomial-time alpha > 0.87856 approximation. Same problem, opposite directions of bound; together they sandwich Max-Cut's approximability between 0.87856 and 0.941. Tagged 'analogous' because the theorems play opposite roles (lower bound vs upper bound) on the same problem.

Complementary MAX DICUT bounds. Hastad TP365.27: NP-hard to approximate within 13/12 - epsilon (i.e., better than ~0.923). Goemans-Williamson AP366.5: polynomial-time beta > 0.79607 approximation, with the constant beta defined in DP366.9 and the key inequality in LP366.7.3.2. Same problem, complementary results.

Complementary MAX 2SAT (Max-E2-Sat) bounds. Hastad TP365.17 shows NP-hardness within 22/21 - epsilon (~0.954). Goemans-Williamson AP366.3 + TP366.7.2.1.1 give an alpha > 0.87856 polynomial-time approximation for MAX 2SAT. Same problem; lower vs upper bound.

Hastad TP365.12 (NP-hard to approximate Max-E3-Sat within 8/7 - epsilon) and TP365.14 (satisfiable instances cannot be distinguished from 7/8+epsilon-satisfiable) bound MAX 3SAT/MAX SAT hardness. Goemans-Williamson AP366.4 gives a 0.7584-approximation for MAX SAT (clauses of any length) using SDP plus probabilistic rounding. The MAX SAT/MAX 3SAT framing differs slightly; both are complementary results on the satisfiability-maximization problem.

Both papers introduce the standard performance-ratio definition for approximation algorithms on maximization problems: a polynomial-time algorithm whose output is at least 1/C (resp. p) times the optimum. Paper A normalizes ratios as C >= 1 (OPT/C <= V <= OPT), paper B as p <= 1 (V >= p * OPT); these are reciprocal conventions for the same notion.
Max-Ek-Lin-2 (linear equations mod 2) is a problem central to Hastad's paper but absent from Goemans-Williamson, which does not consider linear-equation maximization.
Vertex Cover is one of Hastad's target problems (TP365.25) but is not addressed by Goemans-Williamson.
Ek-Set Splitting is paper A specific; not considered in Goemans-Williamson.

Generic CSP definitions (Max-CSP-P, weight w(P,k), non-approximability beyond random-assignment threshold) form Hastad's abstract framework for stating optimal hardness; no analogue in Goemans-Williamson, which only treats specific problems via SDP.
e-satisfiable CNF formula is a paper-A specific definition for the gap-CNF instances used in PCP reductions; no counterpart in Goemans-Williamson.

Folding over true, conditioning upon h, long Gamma-code, Standard Written Proof SWP(u), and Max-Ek-Lin-Gamma are all paper-A-internal machinery for the Long-code/PCP construction. None of these appear in Goemans-Williamson, which uses SDP rather than PCP techniques.

The random-assignment performance theorem (any CSP admits a w(P,k)^{-1}-approximation via conditional expectations) is paper A's baseline; paper B's baselines are different (SDP relaxation values), and there is no direct analogue.

Hastad's flagship Max-Ek-Lin-2 / Max-Ek-Lin-Gamma inapproximability theorems (factor 2 for k>=3, |Gamma| for k=3) have no counterpart in Goemans-Williamson, which does not address linear-equation problems.
Max-E2-Lin-2 hardness within 12/11 - epsilon. Goemans-Williamson does not directly approximate Max-E2-Lin-2; the closest match would be MAX 2SAT, but Max-E2-Lin-2 is a distinct problem.
CSPs implied by linearity (3 bits, k bits) are abstract Hastad results extending Max-E3-Lin-2 hardness; no Goemans-Williamson analogue.

Satisfiable-instance hardness for Max-E4-Sat (15/16+epsilon) and Max-Ek-Sat for k>=4 (1-2^{-k}+epsilon). Goemans-Williamson's AP366.4 (.7584 MAX SAT approximation) is a partial complementary upper bound but the connection is loose; flagged as 'none' to keep the alignment honest.

CSP hardness for disjunctions of length >=3 (TP365.16), 4-variable predicates with prescribed accepting set (TP365.18), and the OXR predicate (TP365.19). All are paper-A-specific; not addressed in Goemans-Williamson.
Hastad's E4-Set Splitting and 4-CSP hardness theorems (8/7, satisfiable variants, monotone variants, negation-allowed). No counterpart in Goemans-Williamson.
Vertex Cover hardness within 7/6 - delta. Goemans-Williamson does not address Vertex Cover.
Hastad's subconstant-epsilon strengthenings (Max-E3-Lin-2, Max-E4-Sat, Max-E3-Sat under quasi-polynomial assumptions). Paper-A-specific; no counterpart in Goemans-Williamson.
Soundness of basic and u-parallel two-prover protocols. Internal Hastad PCP machinery; no SDP analogue.

A Cauchy-Schwarz-style power inequality used in Hastad's Fourier soundness proofs. Goemans-Williamson uses different analytic tools (arccos lower bound LP366.3.4 plays an analogous numerical-bound role but for a different inequality).
Completeness/soundness lemmas for the linearity tests L^epsilon_2(u), L^epsilon_{2,-1}(u), L^epsilon_Gamma(u). Hastad-internal PCP test analyses with no GW analogue.
Character-sum identity for Abelian groups; Hastad-specific tool for the Gamma-code analysis.
Completeness/soundness lemmas for Tests 4S(u), 3S^epsilon(u), F3S^delta(u), and supporting Markov-type tail bounds (LP365.16, CP365.1). All Hastad-internal PCP machinery; no SDP counterpart.
Set-splitting test analyses (SS^epsilon(u), PSS^epsilon(u), FSS^delta(u)) and supporting nonnegativity / multilinear lemmas. Hastad-internal; no GW analogue.
Markov-style tail corollary for S_U; internal to Hastad's Max-E3-Sat satisfiable proof.
Basic and u-parallel two-prover protocols for the verifier-prover gap. No counterpart in Goemans-Williamson, which has no PCP/protocol component.

All of Hastad's PCP tests (L^epsilon_2(u), L^epsilon_{2,-1}(u), L^epsilon_Gamma(u), 4S(u), 3S^epsilon(u), F3S^delta(u), SS^epsilon(u), PSS^epsilon(u), FSS^delta(u)). These are PCP verification algorithms with no analogue in Goemans-Williamson, whose only algorithms are the SDP+hyperplane-rounding approximation algorithms.

Approximate Max-E3-Lin-2, Max-E3-Sat, Vertex Cover (Hastad's targeted approximation problems). Vertex Cover and Max-E3-Lin-2 have no GW counterpart; Max-E3-Sat is partly addressed by AP366.4 but treated under MAX SAT framing rather than E3-Sat specifically.

Hastad's proofs for the inapproximability theorems (Max-E3-Lin-2, soundness of Test L_2, Max-E4-Sat satisfiable, Max-E3-Sat satisfiable, E4-Set Splitting, Vertex Cover). All proceed via PCP+Fourier reductions; no analogue in Goemans-Williamson, whose proofs use SDP duality and spherical geometry.

Boolean Fourier inversion and Parseval identity. These are standard tools used throughout Hastad's analysis; Goemans-Williamson does not use Boolean Fourier analysis (it uses Euclidean / spherical geometry instead).
Hastad's open problems concern classification of CSP predicates; GW's open problems concern combinatorial 0.878-approximation and tighter SDPs. The questions are unrelated.

The constant alpha = min_theta (2/pi)*theta/(1-cos theta) > 0.87856 is GW's central performance-guarantee constant. There is no counterpart in Hastad: his hardness factor for Max-Cut is 17/16 ~ 0.941, derived from a totally different (PCP) construction.

GW's integer quadratic program (Q), vector relaxation (P), semidefinite program (SD), and dual SDP (D) are the SDP machinery underlying the 0.878-approximation. Hastad uses no SDP; the analogue 'relaxation' on his side is the PCP gap, which is structurally unrelated.
MAX RES CUT (cut with same-side / different-side constraints) is a GW-specific application of constrained SDP rounding. Not addressed by Hastad.

Expected cut value formula (E[W] = sum w_ij * arccos(u_i.u_j)/pi) and the underlying hyperplane-separation probability (Pr[separated] = arccos(u_i.u_j)/pi). Core GW analysis steps; Hastad has no continuous/spherical analogue.

GW's arccos numerical inequalities used to prove the alpha bound. Hastad has analogous-in-role numerical lemmas (LP365.3, LP365.16) but for completely different inequalities; matching these across papers would be misleading.
Refined GW bound when MAX CUT is large (h(A) curve via Jensen). GW-specific refinement; no Hastad analogue.
GW's bound for negative-weight Max-Cut; no Hastad analogue.
Z_R^* = Z_{MC}^* equivalence between the nonlinear arccos program and Max-Cut value. GW-specific structural identity.
Three-vector same-sign probability formula via spherical-triangle area (Girard). GW-specific three-vector geometry; Hastad has no spherical-geometry component.
MAX RES CUT (constrained variant). GW-specific.

GW's proofs (hyperplane separation probability via spherical digon, alpha numerical bound, large-A refined bound, R-MC equivalence, three-vector probability, three-vector inequality for MAX DICUT). All use spherical / Euclidean geometry; Hastad's proofs use Long-code Fourier analysis. No proof-level alignment.
GW's open problems (combinatorial .878-approximation without SDP; tighter SDP relaxations) are SDP-method specific, with no counterpart in Hastad's open problems on CSP-predicate classification.
